why:
I checked each verifier PASS and FAIL condition against the words of its expect line.

Check 1 requires clamp to be an exported function that returns lo below the range, hi above it and x inside it. Inclusive bounds and the lo==hi case follow from "limited to the range lo to hi", so nothing stricter is added.

Check 2 requires calls with lo > hi to throw an instance of RangeError, which is exactly what the line says.

Check 3 passes when README.md names clamp and says what it does. That is narrower than "every function", not stricter, so it doesn't break the criterion.

Check 4 asks for exit 0 and zero failing tests. That is what "npm test passes" means; a cancelled test already gives a non-zero exit.

The stricter items sit under "Advisory (not part of any PASS or FAIL condition)": clamp tests in test/math.test.js, the file-scope limit, and NaN behaviour. No PASS or FAIL condition goes beyond its line's words.
